text:
Maria (People Ops): Noticing a bunch of interviewers showing as 'available' in the scheduler but calendar invites are being created at times they actually marked busy. Is this a sync problem? :confused:
Sam (Recruiting Ops): Yep, several tickets reported. I saw invites created at 9pm PST even though the interviewer had 'busy' blocks at that time in Google Calendar.
Lee (Recruiter): Hit this with two panels—interviewer declined after invite went out and we had to scramble.
Nina (Scheduler): On my side the ATS availability cache refresh is every 6h. If an interviewer updates calendar in between refreshes, scheduler can still book until the next cache eviction.
Maria (People Ops): Can we tighten that? For panels we need near-real-time.
Sam (Recruiting Ops): We trade off API quota vs freshness. Last year we increased window because of quota spikes. Maybe we can add a write-through check when creating a panel invite: re-query calendar API for conflicts for the specific time slot before confirming.
Ashley (SRE): That sounds fine but watch latency. A sync-per-booking adds ~200-400ms. We can make it optional per-route: aggressive check for panel assignments and default cached for ad-hoc bookings.
Nina (Scheduler): Would also suggest an optimistic hold: when scheduler picks a slot, mark it transiently in Redis for 2m to prevent race. That plus a final calendar check before send should be robust.
Sam (Recruiting Ops): Plan: 1) add final calendar conflict check for panel bookings, 2) transient slot lock for 2m, 3) lower cache TTL from 6h to 1h for interviewers in active hiring teams.
Lee (Recruiter): Works for me. Anything we need SRE to approve?
Ashley (SRE): I'll review the Redis lock pattern for hotspots. Also need a rollout plan: feature flag behind "aggressive_availability_check" and a canary on 10% orgs first.
Maria (People Ops): Can we prioritize urgent teams (sales eng, core infra) for early rollout? They had the worst impact.
Sam (Recruiting Ops): Adding org tags for priority groups. I'll open a small PR and include a migration to reduce TTL for those orgs. Will coordinate the flag flip with Ashley.
calendar-bot: calendar.api.quota_warning  remaining_requests=1200 day_limit=10000
Nina (Scheduler): Also noticed timezone edge-case: interviewers with multiple calendars in different TZs were double-booked when the scheduler picked the wrong calendar. We should prefer primary calendar explicitly.
Sam (Recruiting Ops): Good catch. I'll update lookup to prefer primary calendar id and fall back if busy.
Ashley (SRE): I'll approve the PR and schedule the canary deploy tonight during low traffic window. Monitoring: increase 5xx and invite declines alert for 30m after deployment.
Maria (People Ops): Thanks. Action items: Sam to PR and flag, Nina to add transient lock logic, Ashley to deploy canary and monitor, Sam to document runbook for conflicts. Aim to close by EOD tomorrow.
Lee (Recruiter): Appreciate the quick turnaround. We'll hold off on scheduling big panels until canary is green.
Sam (Recruiting Ops): Filed REQ-4988 "scheduler: final-calendar-check + transient-lock" and added owners. Moving to follow-up.
Maria (People Ops): Noted. Please post status in #people-ops when canary completes.
calendar-bot: job.scheduled  job=canary-deploy window=2026-03-23T22:00:00Z
Ashley (SRE): Canary started. Will report back in this thread.
Sam (Recruiting Ops): Thanks everyone.
Ashley (SRE): Canary healthy after 30m, no spike in declines, locks holding as expected. Rolling to 30% now.
Maria (People Ops): Fantastic closing note: schedule teams can resume panel scheduling for priority groups. Will update hiring leads.
Sam (Recruiting Ops): Closing thread; follow-up ticket linked.
